target: Aver Engine — Physics/Sim + Networking port design (soft-body solver, aerodynamics, fracture/debris, GPU deform, networking) verified against OpenConstructor27 authoritative sources: VehicleDamage.cpp, VehicleAerodynamics.cpp, VehicleSolverAsync.cpp, OCSimCore/oc_sim.cpp, Net/OCNetTypes.h
mustFix: IMPACT WIRE FRAME IS WRONG (determinism-critical). The design sends crash seeds in CAR-LOCAL frame (Impact msg = [f32 lx/ly/lz][f32 nx/ny/nz][f32 speedKmh], and §6.5 'Crash seed | Impact (car-local UDP)'). The authoritative contract Net/OCNetTypes.h FOCImpactEvent mandates the opposite: 'WORLD space; each client applies its OWN bDeformMirrorY (do not pre-mirror on the wire)'. VehicleDamage.cpp confirms the mechanism: OnHit broadcasts OnImpactQualified with world-space Hit.ImpactPoint/Hit.ImpactNormal (line 2864), and ReportImpact (lines 1248-1259) takes a WORLD point/normal and itself does Xf.InverseTransformPosition + the bDeformMirrorY flip. Feeding an already-local, pre-mirrored seed into that reconstruction path double-transforms and double-mirrors, so replicated dents land in the wrong place / diverge across peers. Send impacts WORLD-space and un-mirrored.

IMPACT MESSAGE DROPS PartHint. FOCImpactEvent carries 'uint8 PartHint = 0xFF' documented as load-bearing: '0xFF = let the client pick nearest ... so clients never re-derive nearest-by-bounds and diverge on a tie.' The design's Impact wire form (both directions) has no PartHint field. For fused/multi-solver vehicles this reintroduces the exact nearest-part tie divergence the field exists to prevent. Add PartHint (0xFF sentinel) to the Impact wire form.

OCSERVER SNAPSHOT WIRE FORM OMITS THREE ESSENTIAL FIELDS. The design projects the durable damage snapshot down to only sparse plastic deltas on the wire ('[i32 beamCount]([i32 beamIdx][i16 plasticMm])*', §6.3, 'no broken bitset / detached parts / repair counter'). The authoritative FOCDamageSnapshot (OCNetTypes.h lines 157-168) is defined as YieldedBeams + BrokenBitset + DetachedParts + RepairCounter together, and its stated purpose is 'reconstruct a half-wrecked car for a late joiner ... and to correct drift.' Dropping BrokenBitset/DetachedParts/RepairCounter from the transport means a late joiner cannot reconstruct broken beams, gone parts, or repairs over that channel. It ALSO directly contradicts the design's own §6.6 claim that 'Repair rides the snapshot's repairCounter, never a bare event' — impossible if repairCounter is not in the wire snapshot. Carry all four fields.

DETACH LOSES IMPULSE + MODE. The design represents part detaches only as bare part indices (snapshot detachedParts / §6.5). The authoritative FOCDetachEvent (OCNetTypes.h lines 127-135) carries Impulse (FVector_NetQuantize10) + Mode (EOCDetachMode{DetachWhole,Shatter,PanelShed}) precisely because 'simulated proxies are not simulating, so they cannot derive it locally.' With indices only, replicas cannot launch debris consistently (trajectory) or choose whole-detach vs shatter vs panel-shed. Preserve Impulse + Mode in the detach representation.
corrections: MATERIAL FORMAT IS REINVENTED. The design claims materials carry 10..13 fields with tearStrainTension/tearStrainCompr/density, citing 'the shipped UE parser required exactly 10 while the writer emits 13.' The authoritative parser (VehicleDamage.cpp lines 255-284) requires EXACTLY 10 fields (Name + Stiffness,AxialStiffness,BendForceN,BreakForceN,PlasticStiffness,MaxBend,BendAbsorb,BreakAbsorb + Behavior, with Behavior TERMINAL) and skips any line with !=10. Neither the parser, the phase-2 resolve (lines 496-516), nor the solver has any tearStrain or density concept; per-node 'mass' (InvMass) is derived from beam AxialStiffness (InitSolver lines 632-657), not a material density. Treat the format as the verified 10-field layout with Behavior last; the extra fields are fabricated and Behavior must not move off the terminal position.

SETTLE METRIC OMITS PHASE-1 MOTION. The design's solveStep updates maxMoveSq only from the Gauss-Seidel correction (Phase 3). The authoritative SolveStep also feeds Phase-1 Verlet velocity into MaxMoveSq (VehicleDamage.cpp lines 2264-2265: 'const float VelSq = Vel.SizeSquared(); MaxMoveSq = FMath::Max(MaxMoveSq, VelSq);'). Settle = (DamageTimer<=0) && (MaxMoveSq <= threshold^2) then also accounts for still-integrating nodes. Include the Phase-1 velocity contribution or the port will report 'settled' prematurely (and, via the async worker, park the episode too early).

TEAR-GENERATION BUMP CONDITION. Design §2.6 says the caller bumps tearGeneration 'only when it grows.' The authoritative code bumps on ANY change: 'R.TornCount != LastTornNodeCount' (VehicleDamage.cpp line 2617). Implement '!=' (change), not '>', or a shrink in the torn set (e.g. after repair/net restore) leaves stale holes uncut.

GPU/CPU deform: the design introduces a per-panel 'deformStiffness' folded into Gain. No per-panel deform stiffness exists in the source — the ProcMesh drive uses a single global DeformGain (VehicleDamage.cpp line 1142) plus the MaxBoneDisplacement/DebrisMaxDrop clamps (line 1229, 1143). Keep the global-gain semantics unless a new feature is intended and labelled as such.

Handedness note 'cage->actor flips Y, negates normal.Y, reverses triangle winding' is only partly grounded: the runtime deform mirrors DISPLACEMENT (disp.Y=-disp.Y, line 1141) and binds lookups in Y-mirrored cage space (line 981); it does not negate normal.Y or re-wind triangles at runtime. Those steps belong to the (not-provided) glTF importer and are unverified — do not present them as established runtime conventions.
faithfulnessIssues: Protocol (A) game table (MsgType Join=1 ... ConfigStatus=19) and the whole coordinator/matchmaking table (CoordMsg QueueJoin=1 ... SrvGoodbye=14, oc_match) cannot be validated against any provided authoritative source. The only net source given, OCNetTypes.h, contains NONE of these enums/layouts — it documents the OCNetWire framed-batch (EMsg{None=0,Input=1,Impact=2,Detach=3,Repair=4,Damage=5,Config=6}) plus UE-reflection ToBytes/FromBytes (SerializeBin). The design labels OCNetWire 'UE-internal and the thing being replaced,' yet OCNetTypes.h presents OCNetWire as exactly the external-server bridge API (ServerApplyInbound/ServerCollectOutbound, 'each server tick the app feeds ONE inbound buffer'). So the design's central interop claim (Protocol A preserves server/coordinator wire) is unverifiable and, if the existing server actually speaks OCNetWire, actively broken. This is the largest verification gap and needs the OCServer Wire.cs / coordinator sources to close.
Design contradicts the authoritative impact-frame contract (world vs car-local, PartHint dropped) — see mustFix #1/#2.
Design's OCServer damage snapshot contradicts the authoritative FOCDamageSnapshot field set and the design's own repair-via-repairCounter guarantee — see mustFix #3.
Design's detach representation drops the impulse/mode that FOCDetachEvent carries specifically for non-simulating replicas — see mustFix #4.
Fabricated material fields/discrepancy (tearStrain*/density, '13-field writer') not present anywhere in the authoritative solver — see corrections #1.
soundnessIssues: Determinism story is sound ONLY on the async/fixed-Hz path, which the design should state as mandatory for MP. The authoritative sync path runs SolveStep with C.Dt = frame DeltaTime (BuildSolveConfig(DeltaTime), VehicleDamage.cpp line 2612) — a VARIABLE, frame-rate-dependent dt. The async worker is fixed-step (1/ResolveSolverHz, which becomes NetSendHz in MP; lines 240/273/2481). The reconstruct-the-end-state model tolerates this because damage only accrues while DamageTimer>0 and DamageTimer decrements by the fixed Step (VehicleSolverAsync.cpp line 281), so total damage steps = ceil(window/step) independent of wall-clock. The design's §2.11 'fixed dt on the authoritative path' is therefore correct but the port MUST forbid the variable-dt sync path as authoritative in MP; make this an explicit invariant, not an implication.

The physics core itself is architecturally faithful and sound: POD index-parallel data model, phase order (Verlet -> damage/plasticity -> Gauss-Seidel per substep), the absolute-deformation force law (Mag = |AxialStiffness * (Len-RestLength)|, NOT strain-normalized), InitSolver (minZ pin band, StructuralStrength applied at init not parse, brittle vote, stiffness-derived InvMass), the OCCrushCurve soft-knee impact injection writing PrevPosition (rate-limited by MaxNodeSpeed), impact-tear radius, chassis rebound (-e*Vn), connectivity recount, repair reset, and the aero attitude derivation + edge-clamped trilinear (force AND CoP) all match the source. oc_sim.cpp is correctly characterized as a P0 forward-motion stub to be preserved and extended in P2. The single-transform world<->local coupling (GetCageTransform, lines 673-681) is cited accurately. These parts are ready to build against; the failures are concentrated in the networking layer and the invented material format.
